newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels say no more hostage releases for now.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels say no more hostage releases for now.

text.p: Peruvian rebels holding 74 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima ruled out on Thursday any imminent release of more captives.
"For now, there are no releases," Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini shouted at journalists outside the residence with a megaphone.

Cerpa took up the megaphone after his efforts to read a statement to reporters via walkie-talkie were foiled by heavy distortion. Reporters at the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence suspected Peruvian police were jamming the frequency used by the rebels.

Cerpa asked for Red Cross visits to jailed members of his Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) to be resumed and called for a sign of "goodwill" from the government of President Alberto Fujimori.

"We think that only in this way can a suitable atmosphere be created for beginning dialogue," Cerpa said. "We hope there is goodwill from the government so that by Feb. 17 (Peruvian Foreign Minister) Francisco Tudela will be out".

Tudela, the prize hostage of the rebels, had been due to attend a crucial round of peace talks in Rio de Janeiro on Feb. 17 to try and resolve Peru and Ecuador's bitter border dispute, which led to a brief war in 1995.
